claim.markdown_says:
Old_South_Arabian:
10A60-10A7C Old_Turkic:   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49374) ... then page-1220 opens with the bare line '10C00-10C48' with no label
claim.why_it_matters: The 'Old_Turkic:' label from the top of PDF page 1190 is concatenated onto Old_South_Arabian's range line; Old_Turkic's range '10C00-10C48' opens the next page with no label.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered pages. PDF page 1219 (printed folio 1189) ends its UCS script-range list with exactly two lines, 'Old_South_Arabian:' then '10A60-10A7C', and nothing follows before the footer. PDF page 1220 (printed folio 1190) opens its body with 'Old_Turkic:' on the first line and '10C00-10C48' on the second. The markdown breaks that pairing: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:49374 reads '10A60-10A7C Old_Turkic:' as a single line, and the page-1220 block (anchor at :49376 ff.) opens with a bare '10C00-10C48' carrying no label. Both quotations in the claim are accurate. I considered rejecting this as page-break furniture or line-wrapping, and rejected that reading: no characters are lost and reading order is preserved, but this table's entire semantic content IS the label-to-range binding, and here that binding is broken in both directions at once - Old_South_Arabian's range line acquires a spurious trailing token, and Old_Turkic's range is orphaned from its name. Any consumer extracting script ranges from the markdown mis-parses two entries. That is a content defect, not formatting. Severity 'structural' is the right grade: record boundaries are corrupted, no glyphs are missing. The claim's only inaccuracy is cosmetic - it cites the following page by its printed folio ('p1190') while heading the finding with the PDF index (1219); PDF page 1220 == printed folio 1190.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED. At the 1219->1220 page boundary the newline separating the last range line of page 1219 from the first label of page 1220 is collapsed to a space, gluing the next entry's label onto the previous entry's range: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:49374 reads '10A60-10A7C Old_Turkic:' where the PDF has '10A60-10A7C' as the terminal line of page 1219 (printed 1189) and 'Old_Turkic:' as the first line of page 1220 (printed 1190). Consequently the page-1220 block opens with an unlabelled '10C00-10C48'. No text is lost and reading order is preserved; the defect is the broken label-to-range pairing, which corrupts two adjacent entries of the UCS script-range table. NOTE - this is not a one-off: it is a systematic transcription artifact at page boundaries inside this table. The immediately preceding boundary carries the identical defect - specs/ISO_COBOL.md:49319 reads '16A40-16A5E, 16A60-16A69 Multani:' (Mro's range with page 1219's opening 'Multani:' label glued on), leaving page 1219's markdown to open with a bare '11280-11286, 11288, 1128A-1128D, 1128F-1129D, 1129F-112A8'. The remedy should be a sweep over every page boundary in this script-range list, not a single-line patch.
